vopros: How do I get AI assistants to recommend my company to customers in the US?

vyzhimka.tekst:
There’s no guaranteed way to make an AI assistant recommend your company. The practical goal is to make your business easy to find, verify, and understand—and to give assistants and their underlying search systems accurate, useful information to draw on.

### Start with the basics

1. **Make your site accessible to search crawlers.** Check that important pages aren’t blocked by `robots.txt`, login walls, or your hosting/CDN setup, and that they return successfully and can be indexed. For ChatGPT Search, OpenAI says sites should allow **OAI-SearchBot**; its search crawler is separate from **GPTBot**, which controls potential use of site content for training. Check crawler access and published IP ranges with your technical team.

2. **Explain your offering clearly on your website.** Create straightforward pages for what you do, who you serve, where you operate, pricing or service details where appropriate, and how you differ. Include specific, verifiable facts—not just broad marketing claims. Keep key information in readable text.

3. **Publish genuinely useful, original material.** Answer the questions customers actually ask, and include firsthand expertise, examples, data, and sources where relevant. Keep pages current. Avoid mass-producing thin pages or repeating keywords; those tactics can undermine trust and search visibility.

4. **Build a consistent, trustworthy presence elsewhere.** Keep your business profiles and directories accurate, encourage honest customer reviews, and seek legitimate coverage or mentions from relevant industry sources. Make sure your business name, location, services, and contact details agree across sources.

5. **Use standard SEO and structured data appropriately.** Good technical SEO, internal links, and valid structured data can help search systems understand your site. Google says its AI search features use the same foundational SEO practices and don’t require special AI markup or files. Structured data should match what visitors can actually see; it does not guarantee a recommendation.

6. **Measure and improve.** Monitor search indexing and website analytics, including referrals from AI search where available. OpenAI says ChatGPT referral URLs include `utm_source=chatgpt.com`. Periodically test realistic customer questions in several assistants, note what they get wrong or omit, and improve the underlying public information.

Treat AI visibility as an extension of good search and reputation work—not as a promise of placement. Avoid paying for supposed guaranteed AI recommendations or trying to manipulate answers with fake reviews, fabricated claims, or spammy content.

results.snippet:
Google Search Central's core guidance on AI Overviews is that there is no special AI-Overviews markup or separate AI index.
The same helpful, people-first, high-quality content and standard structured data that ranks in organic Search is what surfaces in AI Overviews, drawn from the same index and judged by the same E-E-A-T signals.
...
Google has stated that AI Overviews draw from the same index that powers traditional search results.
There is no separate "AI index" or "AI ranking algorithm."
Content that performs well in organic search has a higher baseline probability of being cited in AI Overviews.
...
On content quality, Google Search Central's guidance aligns with their long-standing E-E-A-T framework: Experience, Expertise, Authoritativeness, and Trustworthiness.
Content demonstrating first-hand experience, subject matter expertise, and authoritative sourcing is preferred by the AI Overview system.
...
Google has not published detailed technical specifications for how AI Overviews select specific sources from their index.
...
Google Search Central has long recommended structured data for helping Google understand content.
Schema markup -- Article, FAQ, HowTo, Organization, Author -- provides machine-readable context that any AI system, including AI Overviews, can use to evaluate and categorize your content.
...
No schema type guarantees AI Overview citation.
Structured data helps Google understand your content, which can improve citation likelihood, but it is not a citation trigger.
...
No. Google Search Central does not publish any special markup or schema for AI Overviews.
AI Overviews draw from the same index as organic Search, so the standard structured data and helpful, people-first content that Google already recommends is what makes content eligible for AI Overview citation.
...
Yes, though no schema type guarantees AI Overview citation.
Standard structured data like Article, FAQPage, and Organization schema helps Google understand your content, which can improve citation likelihood as a supporting signal.

OpenAI uses web crawlers (“robots”) and user agents to perform actions for its products, either automatically or triggered by user request.
OpenAI uses OAI-SearchBot and GPTBot robots.txt tags to enable webmasters to manage how their sites and content work with AI.
Each setting is independent of the others – for example, a webmaster can allow OAI-SearchBot in order to appear in search results while disallowing GPTBot to indicate that crawled content should not be used for training OpenAI’s generative AI foundation models.
...
For search results, please note it can take ~24 hours from a site’s robots.txt update for our systems to adjust.
...
|OAI-SearchBot|OAI-SearchBot is for search.
OAI-SearchBot is used to surface websites in search results in ChatGPT’s search features.
Sites that are opted out of OAI-SearchBot will not be shown in ChatGPT search answers, though can still appear as navigational links.
To help ensure your site appears in search results, we recommend allowing OAI-SearchBot in your site’s robots.txt file and allowing requests from our published IP ranges below.
...
Please use OAI-SearchBot in robots.txt for managing Search opt outs and automatic crawl.
